## What OP-10 measures

**OP-10 — Abdomen CT Use of Contrast Material** reports the percentage of a hospital's outpatient abdominal CT examinations performed both with and without contrast. Looking at both sets of images can be clinically appropriate in some situations, so a higher percentage is not, by itself, proof of poor care.

This CMS measure concerns one specific CT practice; it is not a measure of every CT scan or of overall hospital quality. The charts below show hospitals with an available OP-10 score in the July 1, 2024–June 30, 2025 reporting period.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

imaging_url <- "https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/sites/default/files/resources/d0134a9a89e59d49426cf5a2ad063b60_1792599881/Outpatient_Imaging_Efficiency-Hospital.csv"

ct_scores <- read_csv(imaging_url, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(`Measure ID` == "OP-10", Score != "Not Available") |>
  mutate(Score = as.numeric(Score))
```


## OP-10 at a Glance

Before exploring the charts, these summary statistics show how the reported abdominal CT percentages vary across hospitals.

```{r}
#| results: asis

ct_stats <- ct_scores |>
  summarise(
    hospitals = n_distinct(`Facility ID`),
    median_score = median(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25 = quantile(Score, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75 = quantile(Score, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

cat('<div class="imaging-stats">')

cat(sprintf(
  '<div class="imaging-stat"><strong>%s</strong><span>Hospitals reporting OP-10</span></div>',
  format(ct_stats$hospitals, big.mark = ",")
))

cat(sprintf(
  '<div class="imaging-stat"><strong>%.1f%%</strong><span>Median reported OP-10 score</span></div>',
  ct_stats$median_score
))

cat(sprintf(
  '<div class="imaging-stat"><strong>%.1f%%–%.1f%%</strong><span>Middle 50%% of hospital scores</span></div>',
  ct_stats$q25,
  ct_stats$q75
))

cat('</div>')
```

The middle 50% of hospitals provides a useful picture of typical variation, without allowing a small number of unusually high percentages to dominate the comparison.

These statistics describe reported CT imaging practices. They do not establish whether an individual scan was clinically appropriate.

---

## Distribution across hospitals

Each bar represents the number of reporting hospitals in a score range. The interactive chart lets you inspect individual bins; the percentage is the CMS-reported score, not a patient-level rate calculated here.

```{r}
plot_ly(
  data = ct_scores,
  x = ~Score,
  type = "histogram",
  xbins = list(size = 1.5),
  marker = list(color = "#167d8d")
) |>
  layout(
    title = "OP-10 Abdomen CT Scores Across Hospitals",
    xaxis = list(title = "Reported OP-10 percentage (%)"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Number of hospitals")
  )
```

## Compare median scores by state or territory

This chart summarizes reporting hospitals with a median for each state or territory. It is descriptive: differences do not account for patient mix, clinical reasons for imaging, or other factors.

```{r}
ct_by_state <- ct_scores |>
  group_by(State) |>
  summarise(
    median_score = median(Score),
    hospitals = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(median_score)

plot_ly(
  data = ct_by_state,
  x = ~median_score,
  y = ~reorder(State, median_score),
  type = "bar",
  orientation = "h",
  marker = list(color = "#167d8d"),
  text = ~paste0("Hospitals with scores: ", hospitals),
  hovertemplate = "%{y}<br>Median: %{x:.1f}%<br>%{text}<extra></extra>"
) |>
  layout(
    title = "Median OP-10 Score by State or Territory",
    xaxis = list(title = "Median reported percentage (%)"),
    yaxis = list(title = "State or territory"),
    margin = list(l = 80),
    height = 950
  )
```

For measure specifications and source data, see the [CMS Outpatient Imaging Efficiency dataset](https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/dataset/wkfw-kthe).
